value.title: KFX developer platform
value.summary: KFX lets developers add inspectable views, adapters, services, Profiles, and Suites without turning package identity into runtime authority.
value.firstValue: Use the installed Agent-first authoring kit to scaffold, validate, build, and qualify an inert extension before native admission.
value.authorityBoundary: This bundle is a documentation projection. Core KFX, KFD, Work, Warrant, capability, lifecycle, and Release Passport sources retain authority.

sources.nonClaim: Architecture prose does not admit or launch a KFX.
Author guidance does not grant runtime capabilities.
A valid package declaration is an input, not execution authority.
Registry projection is not an independent lifecycle journal or generation authority.
Capability ownership does not imply a grant to any package.
Surface neutrality does not collapse physical host isolation boundaries.
A Suite dependency graph is not installation or activation authority.
The stable host contract does not authorize a listener or expose credentials.
Installed discovery metadata does not make an extension qualified.
Scaffold, build, and qualification commands do not install or activate a package.
Catalog availability does not bypass command mutation policy.
Release Passport evidence proves a declared release boundary, not runtime permission.
Retained terminal qualification does not promote KFX to stable or authorize a new package.
Reference observations do not mutate GitHub, admit Issues, or complete Work.
Suite membership does not grant component capabilities.
Profile closure is not production endpoint or secret configuration.
Local content and runtime checks do not prove a real GitHub canary.

facets.title: Why KFX
facets.summary: Extend Kungfu through inspectable, rooted packages while Core retains admission and runtime authority.
facets.nonClaim: KFX is not a trust shortcut for first-party or bundled code.

facets.title: Architecture and hosts
facets.summary: Views, adapters, and services have distinct physical hosts and preserve one Core descriptor.
facets.nonClaim: Presentation parity does not merge renderer, injected adapter, and service isolation.

facets.title: Packages and facets
facets.summary: The versioned KFX manifest declares package identity, facets, requested capabilities, and host inputs; retained qualification covers package, install, activation, upgrade, rollback, and removal for the maintained webhook suite.
facets.nonClaim: A conforming manifest remains inert until native admission.

facets.title: Registry, admission, and lifecycle
facets.summary: A pinned Fact cut, Work, Warrant, policy, exact roots, and CAS guard every accepted package, install, activation, upgrade, rollback, and removal mutation.
facets.nonClaim: Filesystem discovery and package metadata are observations, not registry authority.

facets.title: Capabilities and confinement
facets.summary: Packages request capabilities; Core policy and an explicit exact grant select the allowed subset for one host and preserve that separation across upgrade and rollback.
facets.nonClaim: Declaration, KFD success, or package origin does not grant a capability.

facets.title: KFD and Release Passport trust
facets.summary: KFD, the exact Release Passport, and installed-product lifecycle receipts provide bounded conformance evidence before Core admission.
facets.nonClaim: Qualification and release evidence are eligibility inputs, not execution permission or proof that the optional real GitHub canary ran.

facets.title: Installed Agent-first authoring
facets.summary: The installed, version-matched kit supports scaffold, inspect, validate, build, offline qualify, package, install, activate, upgrade, rollback, and remove steps.
facets.nonClaim: Authoring output remains inert; lifecycle commands require their declared native admission and do not expose a public listener by themselves.

facets.title: SDK and CLI surfaces
facets.summary: The runtime SDK projection and public CLI catalog expose version-matched authoring, lifecycle, and native inspection routes.
facets.nonClaim: A visible CLI route does not change its declared mutation or approval policy.

facets.title: Profiles and Suites
facets.summary: Profiles compose domain contracts and qualification; Suites declare required and optional member dependency closure, including the maintained webhook ingress, view, and dormant bridge.
facets.nonClaim: Dependency closure does not install, activate, or widen a member.

facets.title: GitHub Webhook reference suite
facets.summary: A maintained service/view/optional-bridge suite demonstrates authenticated intake, inspectable evidence, and dormant optional integration.
facets.nonClaim: The retained local qualification is not a deployed public webhook or real-secret canary.

facets.title: Current qualification status
facets.summary: Identity-neutral terminal evidence and the maintained webhook Profile cover installed-product package, lifecycle, rollback, removal, and local reference-suite qualification.
facets.nonClaim: Current retained evidence does not establish stable compatibility, downstream Site adoption, or completion of the optional real GitHub/AWS China canary.

nonClaims: The dedicated KFX Site Bundle is a deterministic documentation projection, not a registry, permission system, lifecycle authority, or maturity oracle.
This source change does not publish @kungfu-tech/site or any other npm package.
The production KFX Site does not consume this bundle until a separately reviewed downstream adoption.
No source-built or retained qualification evidence opens a stable KFX compatibility line.
